# Copilot review instructions

Pure .NET repo — Roslyn analyzers + code fixes targeting `netstandard2.0`. No Node/npm.
The engineering contract lives in `AGENTS.md` (root `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it); defer
to it for conventions rather than duplicating them here.

## Reviewer focus

- Review **the changes in this PR**, not the whole repo. The diff is the assignment.
- Skip generated/derived files — review the generator, not its output:
  - `*.g.cs`, `*.Designer.cs`, and anything whose first lines say `<auto-generated>` / `// Generated`.
  - `bin/`, `obj/`, `artifacts/`.
  - the generated catalog under `docs/` (`ANcpLua.Analyzers.md`, `docs/rules/*`, `*.sarif`,
    `docs/editorconfig/*`) — produced by `tools/ANcpLua.Analyzers.DocsGenerator` and guarded by
    its `--check` mode in CI.

## Coordinate with other reviewers

- Codex (`chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`) reviews the same PRs and its approval gates auto-merge.
  Read its comments first and **don't repeat findings it already raised**; don't re-raise
  anything the author has marked resolved.

## Style

- When there are more than ~5 findings, group them by file, not by severity.
- Don't suggest renaming public surface (diagnostic IDs, descriptor/symbolic names, public API)
  without a concrete caller-side benefit — consumers, the docs generator, and the `HelpLinkUri`
  URLs all depend on those names.
- Don't suggest tests "for completeness" — only when a changed contract is genuinely uncovered.
  Each rule is pinned by `AnalyzerTest<T>` cases.

## Project conventions

Defer to `AGENTS.md`. The ones most worth enforcing in review:

- Central Package Management; `Version.props` is the single owner of versions — never edit
  `<Version>` / `<PackageVersion>` directly. `LangVersion` / `Nullable` are SDK-owned.
- Per-analyzer `const string DiagnosticId` — no central `DiagnosticIds` class.
- Prefer `ANcpLua.Roslyn.Utilities` helpers (`.IsEqualTo`, `.Implements`, `context.ReportDiagnostic`)
  over manual `SymbolEqualityComparer` / base-type walks / raw `Diagnostic.Create`.

## Rate-limit / failure behavior

If you hit a rate limit, **surface the limit and its unblock date in the review body** rather
than a generic "encountered an error" — the author needs the date to plan.
